headline: Tigresses eye semi-final berth in crucial T20I clash against Sri Lanka today
summary: Bangladesh takes on Sri Lanka in a pivotal T20I match today, with a win securing their spot in the tournament's semi-finals. Batting improvements are key on the tricky Dubai pitch.
details: Bangladesh will look to book their place in the semi-finals when they take on Sri Lanka in their second Group B match of the tournament at the Dubai International Cricket Stadium today. A victory would confirm their spot in the semifinals.

Although Bangladesh opened their campaign with a commanding 71-run victory over Indonesia, their batting performance, managing only 129-8, left room for improvement. Apart from Shorna Akter's unbeaten 18-ball 31, other batters struggled.
Batting coach Nasiruddin Faruque is not concerned, noting the tricky Dubai surface makes stroke-making difficult. He suggested that a total around 140 could prove competitive on such wickets.

Faruque emphasized the need to utilize the powerplay and build strong partnerships in the middle overs to post a decent score. He also pointed out Sri Lanka's struggles against Indonesia, scoring 124-7.

Opener Juairiya Ferdous echoed confidence, stating that the experience from their opening game would significantly benefit them against Sri Lanka. She believes a win would be a massive step towards their ultimate goal.

Sri Lanka currently leads Group B with four points from two matches, while Bangladesh is second with two points from one game and a net run rate of +3.550. Hosts UAE are third with two points from two matches.

Historically, Sri Lanka has a dominant record against Bangladesh in T20Is, winning 13 out of 16 encounters. Bangladesh's last victory against Sri Lanka was in 2023, followed by six consecutive T20I losses.

headline: Businessman shot in Dhaka shop, attacker caught by locals
summary: A businessman named Aslam Khan was shot inside his crockery shop in Shonir Akhra, Dhaka. He sustained injuries to his left arm and right cheek and is currently hospitalized.
details: A businessman, Aslam Khan (38), was shot and injured inside his crockery shop in Shonir Akhra, Kadamtali, Jatrabari, Dhaka, on Saturday night around 8 PM.
According to his cousin Miraj Khan, Aslam was speaking with a customer when an individual entered the shop and fired at him. He was hit in his left arm and right cheek.
Aslam Khan was initially taken to a local hospital before being transferred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) for further treatment.
Locals apprehended the attacker as he attempted to flee the scene after the shooting. He was subsequently handed over to the police, though his identity has not yet been released.
The motive behind the shooting remains unclear, and Aslam Khan's relatives have not been able to provide any information regarding why he was targeted.
caption:
A businessman was shot inside his shop in Dhaka's Shonir Akhra on Saturday night. Locals apprehended the attacker as he tried to flee the scene.

A businessman, Aslam Khan (38), was shot and injured inside his crockery shop in Shonir Akhra, Kadamtali, Jatrabari, Dhaka, on Saturday night around 8 PM.

According to his cousin Miraj Khan, Aslam was speaking with a customer when an individual entered the shop and fired at him. He was hit in his left arm and right cheek.

Aslam Khan was initially taken to a local hospital before being transferred to Dhaka Medical College Hospital (DMCH) for further treatment.

Locals apprehended the attacker as he attempted to flee the scene after the shooting. He was subsequently handed over to the police, though his identity has not yet been released.

The motive behind the shooting remains unclear, and Aslam Khan's relatives have not been able to provide any information regarding why he was targeted.
